864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .
